# nexus piholerecord remove

Delete a local A record

Deletes an A record's line. Works on unzoned records too. An unknown record answers 404 not-found and a duplicate one 409 conflict. Restarts DNS. When a record line changes, the new configuration is tested (pihole-FTL --test), DNS is fully restarted once (pihole restartdns: a brief outage for every client), and each changed name is checked against 127.0.0.1; any failure restores the previous file and restarts DNS again. Fails dns-config-test-failed, dns-verification-failed or pihole-command-failed, each with rolledBack, and dns-rollback-failed, naming the rollback copy, when even the restore's restart fails (DNS may be down). The file is replaced atomically; the first Nexus write of it also saves a pre-Nexus backup, reported as preNexusBackup. ifMatch, when given, refuses with 409 dns-file-conflict unless the file's etag matches, as does a concurrent edit of the file during the operation. Nexus never writes local= or server= lines. Side effects: atomically rewrites Pi-hole's local DNS records file, saving a pre-Nexus backup on the first Nexus write, then tests the configuration and restarts DNS. Long-running: answers 202 with an operation, queued in order behind every other Pi-hole operation (the pihole lane); it runs as root in its own systemd unit outside nexusd's sandbox, so it survives a restart of nexusd. A queued operation can be canceled; a running one cannot.

## Usage

```
nexus piholerecord remove NAME [flags]
```

## Examples

```
  # Delete a local A record
  nexus piholerecord remove <name>
  # The same, safe to retry
  nexus piholerecord remove <name> --idempotency-key <key>
```

## Flags

```
      --filter stringArray       key=value, repeatable: print only objects whose dot path has this value; a repeated key matches any of its values
      --follow                   stream the operation's output to stderr while waiting
  -h, --help                     help for remove
      --idempotency-key string   Idempotency-Key header: a retry with the same key and input returns the original operation (at most 255 visible ASCII characters)
      --if-match string          Refuse with 409 unless the DNS file's etag is this, sha256:<hex>.
      --no-wait                  print the operation as accepted and exit, without waiting for it to end
  -o, --output string            output format: table, json, jsonl, yaml (default table on a terminal, jsonl otherwise)
      --select strings           print only these dot paths of each object, comma-separated, such as name,properties.state; host and id are always kept
      --stdin                    read JSON Lines objects from stdin, such as another command's output, and run once per line: each binds its host and its id or name; a line without host uses the target host
      --stop-on-error            with --stdin, stop at the first line that fails
      --tag strings              target every configured host with this tag; comma-separated or repeated for any of several
      --timeout duration         stop waiting after this long, such as 90s or 5m, and exit 7; the operation is not canceled
      --yes                      do not ask for confirmation; required to mutate without a terminal
```

## Global flags

      --host string   target hosts: configured names, comma-separated, or all (default: NEXUS_HOST, then the default host)
      --verbose       log each request and response status to stderr
